problems.name: A pot is added the moment it exists
problems.summary: a potter can make a record for a pot that has just been made, with one wet finger, in a few seconds, without having to decide anything.

problems.name: A pot is moved to its next stage
problems.summary: a potter can move a pot on, or put it right if a finger slipped, with one touch or two and without reading much.

problems.name: A photo is added without a clean hand
problems.summary: a potter can take a photo of a pot, a failure or a finished piece with one wet finger, and have it land on the right pot without further sorting.

problems.name: A failed pot is kept with its photo
problems.summary: a potter can mark a pot failed in a moment and keep a photo of it, the stage where it broke, and later why.

problems.name: A shelf or kiln hand-in is checked
problems.summary: a potter can see what is where, and what is out of their hands, in one glance, and move a whole group in a few touches.

problems.name: A wet finger can drive the screen
problems.summary: the controls tolerate a coated, wet or clumsy finger, and what cannot be done then can be done later without loss.

problems.name: An entry made with no signal is trusted
problems.summary: a potter never wonders whether an entry or photo was kept, and never waits on the network to continue.

problems.name: A friend logs a first pot unaided
problems.summary: a friend who receives a link can install the app and log their first pot with nobody explaining anything, and finds the stages already fit how they work.

problems.name: The app feels like a craft object
problems.summary: the app looks and moves like something made by a potter for potters, and is no slower for it.

dimensions.problem: A pot is added the moment it exists
dimensions.name: How a new pot is started

options.name: Photo first, details later
options.description: The home screen's largest control opens the camera, and the photo taken becomes a new pot at the first stage, with the date, and nothing else asked.

options.name: One tap makes a blank pot
options.description: A single large "new pot" control creates a pot at the first stage, dated now, with no photo; the new pot opens so a photo or note can follow.

options.name: Chips for form and method
options.description: After the new-pot tap, one screen offers large chips for form (mug, bowl, vase, plate, other) and method (hand-built, wheel, cast); one touch on each, or skip.

options.name: Copy the last pot
options.description: A control on a pot (or on the home screen, for the latest) makes a new pot with the same form, method, clay and intent, at the first stage.

dimensions.why_it_matters: the entrance is the most repeated touch in the app, and potters who only add pots when it is cheap will keep using it; several entrances could coexist.

dimensions.problem: A pot is added the moment it exists
dimensions.name: How a pot is named and told apart

options.name: No name, the photo is the name
options.description: A pot is shown by its latest photo and its form; no name is asked for or shown unless typed.

options.name: Automatic number and form
options.description: The app names a pot by a running number and its form ("Mug 14"); the potter can rename it.

options.name: A name spoken or typed later
options.description: The pot gets its name at a calm moment, by the phone's dictation key or by typing, from a prompt in the catch-up list.

options.name: A number written on the pot
options.description: The app shows the pot's number in very large type on its screen, so it can be written on the foot or on a tag with a pencil or underglaze; the number is used to open the pot later.

dimensions.why_it_matters: typing is the hardest thing to do with clay on a finger, yet pots of the same form look alike on a shelf.

dimensions.problem: A pot is added the moment it exists
dimensions.name: How a batch of pots is entered

options.name: One record per pot
options.description: Each pot has its own record, always; a batch is several quick adds.

options.name: One record with a count
options.description: A record can say "x 12" and move together; separating one off is a later step.

options.name: A set holding single pots
options.description: A set groups several pot records; moving the set moves each, and any single pot can still leave the set.

dimensions.why_it_matters: the unit of a record (one pot, a batch, a set) decides how many touches a day of making costs.

dimensions.problem: A pot is moved to its next stage
dimensions.name: How the move is made

options.name: A big next-stage button
options.description: Every pot screen has one very large button that names the next stage ("Leather hard ->"); one touch moves the pot.

options.name: Swipe the card on
options.description: In a list, swiping a pot card to the side moves it to the next stage.

options.name: A stage rail to tap
options.description: A rail of the stages sits on the pot screen; touching any stage moves the pot there, so a pot can jump forward or back.

options.name: Drag along a board
options.description: Pots are cards in columns, one per stage, and a card is dragged to another column.

dimensions.why_it_matters: this is the repeated action of the app after adding; the way it is made decides how many touches a shelf walk costs.

dimensions.problem: A pot is moved to its next stage
dimensions.name: How a pot is found to be moved

options.name: Recently touched on top
options.description: The home screen lists pots with the most recently touched or longest-waiting first, each as a large card with its next-stage button.

options.name: A photo grid by stage
options.description: A grid of photos grouped by stage; touching a photo opens the pot.

options.name: Open the pot from a tag
options.description: A pot's number, or a printed code on a tag stuck to a shelf or bat, is read by the camera or typed on a large number pad to open it.

options.name: Search by typing
options.description: A search field finds pots by name, form, clay or glaze.

dimensions.why_it_matters: finding the pot costs as many touches as moving it, and similar pots are hard to tell apart.

dimensions.problem: A pot is moved to its next stage
dimensions.name: How a wrong move is put right

options.name: Undo bar after each move
options.description: After a move, a bar at the bottom says "Moved to Bone dry. Undo" for several seconds; the bar is a large target.

options.name: Hold to move
options.description: The move button fills as it is held (about half a second) and moves only on completion; a touch that slides off cancels.

options.name: Confirm every move
options.description: Touching the button opens a confirm panel with two big buttons.

options.name: Edit the history later
options.description: No protection at the moment; every move is a dated line on the pot, editable or deletable at the sink.

dimensions.why_it_matters: a big target and a slipping wet finger together will produce wrong moves; the cost of putting one right sets how big the targets can be.

dimensions.problem: A pot is moved to its next stage
dimensions.name: What a move records by itself

options.name: Date and stage only
options.description: The move writes the stage and the date, and nothing is asked.

options.name: One optional line after the move
options.description: The move completes at once, then a note field with a dictation key appears for a line that can be ignored.

options.name: A photo nudge on key stages
options.description: On chosen stages (leather hard, bisqued, finished) the move offers a camera button on the next screen, which can be skipped.

options.name: A branch question at forks
options.description: At a fork (after bone dry: bisque, or straight to glaze), the move asks one question with two or three large answers.

dimensions.why_it_matters: what each move asks decides whether it stays one touch; what it records decides how much of the journey survives.

dimensions.problem: A photo is added without a clean hand
dimensions.name: How the camera is reached

options.name: The phone's own camera sheet
options.description: A photo button uses a file input that opens the phone's camera (or its photo picker), and the picture comes back to the app.

options.name: A viewfinder inside the app
options.description: The app shows a live camera view with one huge shutter and keeps the shot with no confirm.

options.name: Photos taken outside, picked after
options.description: The potter takes photos with the phone's camera app, then picks them from the photo library inside the app.

dimensions.why_it_matters: the camera route decides speed, offline behaviour and how much of the phone's own camera the potter keeps.

dimensions.problem: A photo is added without a clean hand
dimensions.name: What the photo attaches to

options.name: The open pot and its stage
options.description: A photo taken from a pot's screen attaches to that pot at its current stage.

options.name: The pot just moved
options.description: After a move, the camera button on the next screen attaches the photo to that move.

options.name: An inbox sorted later
options.description: Every photo lands in an inbox with a time; at the sink the potter drags or taps them onto pots.

dimensions.why_it_matters: a photo that lands on the wrong pot or the wrong stage is a record that cannot be trusted; extra choosing costs touches.

dimensions.problem: A photo is added without a clean hand
dimensions.name: How a photo is taken without tapping

options.name: A countdown shutter
options.description: One touch starts a three- to five-second countdown, then the shot is taken, so the hand can go back to the pot.

options.name: A spoken word as shutter
options.description: The phone listens for a word ("now") and takes the photo.

options.name: The volume button as shutter
options.description: The potter uses the phone's own camera app, where the volume buttons take photos (recalled), then picks the photo in the app.

options.name: Tapping only
options.description: Photos are always taken with a touch on a large shutter.

dimensions.why_it_matters: a photo of a pot held in the other hand needs the finger the shutter wants.

dimensions.problem: A failed pot is kept with its photo
dimensions.name: How a failure is marked

options.name: A failure button on the pot
options.description: A pot screen has a "failed" control away from the next-stage button; it opens a panel with a camera button and large stage and cause chips.

options.name: Failure photo first
options.description: The camera's shutter has a second control, "photograph a failure", which creates or finds the pot, marks it failed at its current stage and keeps the photo.

options.name: Cause chips after marking
options.description: After marking, a row of large chips offers causes drawn from the stage map (drying crack, dunting, crawl, pinholes, glaze ran, broke when handled), one touch or skip.

options.name: Mark now, explain later
options.description: A failure is marked and photographed; the catch-up list asks for the cause and what to change at a calm moment.

dimensions.why_it_matters: Project Memory asks to "see a photo of the failure", and failures are found at unplanned moments, often at the kiln.

dimensions.problem: A shelf or kiln hand-in is checked
dimensions.name: What the first screen shows

options.name: Stage columns
options.description: Pots are grouped by stage, one stage per row or column, with a count.

options.name: Oldest waiting first
options.description: One list ordered by days in the current stage, longest first, each with a next-stage button.

options.name: Photo wall with stage badges
options.description: A wall of recent photos, each with a small stage mark.

options.name: Handed in and not back
options.description: A strip at the top lists what is out of the potter's hands (with staff for bisque or glaze firing), with days waiting, above the other views.

dimensions.why_it_matters: the maintainer did not say what they want to see first at a shelf or the kiln (see Open questions), so the home screen is the biggest unanswered design choice here.

dimensions.problem: A shelf or kiln hand-in is checked
dimensions.name: How a firing hand-in is logged

options.name: Select many then move
options.description: A long press (or a select mode) ticks pots; one move button moves all ticked pots to the next stage.

options.name: A hand-in session
options.description: A "hand in for bisque" mode shows every pot at the stage before bisque with a large check beside each; one button ends the session and moves the checked ones.

options.name: Each pot on its own
options.description: Pots are moved one at a time with the normal next-stage control.

dimensions.why_it_matters: a hand-in or collection moves many pots together, so the per-pot touch count multiplies.

dimensions.problem: A wet finger can drive the screen
dimensions.name: How big and where the controls are

options.name: Thumb-zone slab buttons
options.description: Primary controls are tall bars across the bottom of the screen, well above the 44-point minimum; everything else is smaller and higher.

options.name: Whole-card targets
options.description: Every card on a list is one target; touching anywhere acts (opens the pot), with only one action per card.

options.name: A single huge button per screen
options.description: Every screen has exactly one primary action filling most of it; others are tiny text.

dimensions.why_it_matters: target size trades speed against how much fits on a screen; no source gives a wet-finger size, so it is a choice to test.

dimensions.problem: A wet finger can drive the screen
dimensions.name: When the entry is made

options.name: A one-touch mark at the bench
options.description: At the bench the only possible action is a one-touch mark (a new pot, or a photo); details come later.

options.name: After washing at the sink
options.description: Everything the app can do is meant for clean hands at the sink; the bench has nothing to do.

options.name: A catch-up list for later
options.description: A list of things to finish (unnamed pots, unsorted photos, failures with no cause) is kept, and nothing blocks the potter from ignoring it.

dimensions.why_it_matters: the tools survey's forum accounts say that entering things in arrears is the usual app weakness; whether capture happens at the bench at all is unknown (see Open questions).

dimensions.problem: An entry made with no signal is trusted
dimensions.name: How saving shows when offline

options.name: Silent save with a kept-on-phone mark
options.description: Every entry is saved on the phone at once; a small mark on the card says it is kept on the phone.

options.name: A visible queue count
options.description: A badge counts entries not yet sent anywhere and clears when sent.

options.name: Nothing shown at all
options.description: The app looks the same online and off.

dimensions.why_it_matters: the maintainer works with poor signal; an entry that looks lost, or a pause, will make the potter stop using it.

dimensions.problem: A friend logs a first pot unaided
dimensions.name: How the link opens

options.name: Straight into a working app
options.description: The link opens the app's home screen, usable at once, with no welcome page.

options.name: A one-screen welcome first
options.description: The link opens a single screen that says in a sentence what it is and offers two big buttons: "install it" and "try it".

options.name: Install first, then open
options.description: The link shows only install instructions until the app is installed, and the installed app opens.

dimensions.why_it_matters: the first ten seconds decide whether a friend reaches a pot or closes the tab.

dimensions.problem: A friend logs a first pot unaided
dimensions.name: How home-screen install is taught

options.name: A picture card for your phone
options.description: A card shows the share-menu or browser-menu steps as a drawing for the phone detected, with a single "done" touch.

options.name: Install offered after the first pot
options.description: The card appears only after a first pot is logged, when the friend has a reason.

options.name: Instructions in the message with the link
options.description: The author sends a one-line install note and a picture with the link.

options.name: A native install button where there is one
options.description: Where the browser offers an install prompt, a button in the app triggers it with a single touch.

dimensions.why_it_matters: the maintainer wants a home-screen install; on an iPhone it is a menu route the friend has to be shown.

dimensions.problem: A friend logs a first pot unaided
dimensions.name: How the first pot is led

options.name: An empty page with one button
options.description: The first screen has one button, "your first pot", and nothing else until a pot exists.

options.name: A sample pot to play with
options.description: A sample pot (clearly marked) is already there, and moving it a stage and adding a photo teaches the controls; it can be deleted in one touch.

options.name: A three-step coach on the first pot
options.description: On the first pot only, three short prompts (photo, move on, add the next) point at the controls.

dimensions.why_it_matters: a friend who must ask what to touch has failed the no-help test.

dimensions.problem: A friend logs a first pot unaided
dimensions.name: How a friend's stages are set up

options.name: The default list, edit later
options.description: Every friend starts with the same default stages; renaming, adding and reordering are in a settings page used after the first pot.

options.name: Pick a starting kit
options.description: One screen offers two or three kits (hand-build and fire at a studio, wheel, single firing) and the friend picks one in a touch.

options.name: Build the list at the start
options.description: The friend writes their own stages before the first pot.

dimensions.why_it_matters: the stage names have to fit the friend ("Friends work much like me", but with their own words), and every question asked before the first pot costs a friend.

dimensions.problem: A friend logs a first pot unaided
dimensions.name: How a friend's private space begins

options.name: Space made on the phone by the link
options.description: Opening the link makes an empty private space on that phone; no account.

options.name: A sign-in after the first pot
options.description: The first pot is logged on the phone; the app then offers to keep it safe with a sign-in.

options.name: A code the author gives
options.description: The link carries or is followed by a code the author gives each friend, which opens that friend's private space.

dimensions.why_it_matters: each friend keeps their own private records; how a space is made decides whether a first pot needs an account. This depends on a sign-in and storage decision no Hop has made.

dimensions.problem: The app feels like a craft object
dimensions.name: The look as a whole

options.name: Paper and clay tones
options.description: Warm off-white paper, slip and clay colours (unglazed terracotta, stoneware grey, bisque pink), low contrast edges, one accent.

options.name: Photo-led and nearly bare
options.description: Pots' photos are almost the entire screen; text and buttons are small, plain and sit over or beside the image.

options.name: Glaze colours as the palette
options.description: The app borrows its colours from the potter's own glazes or from the dominant colours of the pot's photo.

options.name: Hand-drawn and ink
options.description: Line drawings of pots as icons and dividers, hand-lettered headings, ink on paper.

dimensions.why_it_matters: the look is something later variations may differ on, and the brief wants "a craft object, not a business product".

dimensions.problem: The app feels like a craft object
dimensions.name: How a stage looks at a glance

options.name: Clay-state colour bands
options.description: A colour band follows the state of the clay: dark wet clay, paler leather hard, chalk-white bone dry, pink bisque, glaze colours, finished.

options.name: A pot silhouette that fills
options.description: A small pot outline fills with clay colour as the pot moves on, with the stage name beside it.

options.name: Plain stage words
options.description: The stage is its name in text, with no mark.

options.name: Stamped seals
options.description: Each stage has a simple stamp-like mark (like a potter's chop), in one ink colour.

dimensions.why_it_matters: the same mark that makes the app feel crafted can show a pot's stage without reading, which helps wet-handed use.

dimensions.problem: The app feels like a craft object
dimensions.name: How an action feels

options.name: Thumbprint press
options.description: When a move is made, a thumbprint-like impression settles into the card and the new stage appears; no waiting.

options.name: Slow settling motion
options.description: Cards ease in, with soft slow movement, as clay settles.

options.name: A small sound or buzz
options.description: A soft sound or a buzz confirms a move, so the potter need not look.

options.name: Plain instant response
options.description: Controls change at once with no ornament.

dimensions.why_it_matters: motion and feedback are the cheapest way to make a quick tool feel made, and the costliest way to make it slow.
